spec.title: vscode PROP-004: Build and test - install, hygiene, watch channels, runners, packaging stamps

status.comment: the type's answer to the build-and-test question of PROP-016 §2; the anchored facts moved verbatim from modules/codkit/PROP-010 in the split of 2026-09-09

p.VSCODE-BUILD-STEPS: The commands the universal `ci --profile build` skeleton calls for this type (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-011#PROFILE-BUILD`, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-CI-IMPL`): the dependency install is `npm ci` of the tree and of `build/` (in CI it is supplied out of band and only its receipts are probed); the hygiene script is `npm run hygiene` and the lint script is `npm run eslint`, and both run **before** the overlay targets are materialized, because upstream hygiene is strict about the manifest it checks; the product and contract tests are `npm run test-node -- --runGlob vs/<ownRoot leaf>/**/test/{common,node}/**/*.test.js`; the package build is the upstream `gulp vscode-*` task. The order of the steps, the profiles and the exit codes are the engine's; the names of the scripts are this type's answer.

p.VSCODE-DEPENDENCY-ROOTS: **The dependency roots of this family are two**: `node_modules/` of the tree and `build/node_modules/` of the build toolchain, because the install of this distribution is two `npm ci` runs (##VSCODE-BUILD-STEPS). That is this type's answer to `build.dependencyRoots` (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-DEPENDENCY-ROOTS`): a tree that restored only the first root is not ready for a build profile, and the run says which receipt is missing. The pair used to be a module constant of the engine; it moved here when a second family met it.

p.BUILD-COMMIT-COMES-FROM-THE-TREE-HEAD: **Build commit.** The product package build (`gulp vscode-*`) stamps `product.json.commit` from `BUILD_SOURCEVERSION`, and without it by reading `.git/HEAD` as a directory (`build/lib/git.ts` at pin 1.135.0); a managed tree is a linked worktree, its `.git` is a file, so the package is left without `commit`, and without `commit` the NLS loader does not read language packs. This is what `build.packageStamps` of this type answers - `BUILD_SOURCEVERSION` from the tree head and `VSCODE_QUALITY` from the quality channel of the patch set, or from the pin tag while it names none (##VSCODE-QUALITY-IS-A-PRODUCT-ANSWER) - and `codkit package` (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-PACKAGE`) is the run that puts them into the environment of the packager. Codkit still neither writes the package nor changes code: it runs the upstream task and stamps what the task reads.

p.VSCODE-BUILD-CHANNELS-DEFAULT: **The default channels of this family are `transpile` and `typecheck`.** Its profile declares four; the other two compile the add-ons and are started by name when a change asks for them. This pair used to be a module constant of the watch wrapper and of the ci engine, which made it the default of every family (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-BUILD-CHANNELS`); it is this type's answer now.

p.VSCODE-QUALITY-IS-A-PRODUCT-ANSWER: **The quality channel is a property of the product, not of the pin it sits on**, so it is the patch set that answers it: `typeConfig.quality`, one of `stable`, `insider`, `exploration`, optional, and stamped into `VSCODE_QUALITY` as the literal word. A patch set that names none keeps the older answer, the tag of the pin - which is a version string (`1.135.0`), and therefore reads as "not the released channel" to every part of the upstream build that compares this variable with `stable`: the packaging of a bundled extension then takes its pre-release path, demands a publish counter it was never given, and the whole `codkit package` run stops. That is how this was measured, on the first real distributable of this family on 2026-09-09. Two things follow and both are recorded here rather than in the engine: the three words are the ones the upstream build itself distinguishes, so a fourth word is a `CK-E-CONFIG` refusal of the schema and never a value handed to a packager; and the operator keeps the last word anyway, because a stamp already exported into the environment is never overwritten (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-STAMPS-FILL-A-GAP`).

p.VSCODE-PACKAGE-SCRATCH: **The packaging of this family rewrites the manifest of a bundled add-on in place**, and a successful `codkit package` therefore used to end with a tracked file of the upstream changed: the add-on's own `package.json` gets its build kind, its version and its pre-release flag written by the bundler of the add-on, and the whole file reformatted. That is what `build.packageScratch` of this type names - `extensions/*/package.json`, the shape of those manifests rather than the name of one add-on, because which add-ons a distribution bundles is the distribution's business and not the type's - so `codkit package` puts them back and `status` calls what is left after an interrupted run packaging residue (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-PACKAGE-SCRATCH`). Measured on 2026-09-09 on the first real distributable, where the run finished green and `codkit status` then advised extracting the bump into the delta. A quality channel of `stable` (##VSCODE-QUALITY-IS-A-PRODUCT-ANSWER) removes the version bump from that rewrite, because the pre-release path is what computes a new version - but not the rewrite itself, which is why the answer does not depend on the channel.

p.VSCODE-PACKAGE-OUTPUTS: **This family names no package output inside the tree, and that is the honest answer.** The `gulp vscode-*` task writes its result into a **sibling** directory of the managed tree whose name carries the platform and the architecture (`../VSCode-<platform>-<arch>*/`), while `build.packageOutputs` is tree-relative by contract (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-PACKAGE-ANSWERS`). Rather than widen the contract so the engine can list a directory it neither manages, guards nor cleans, this type answers with an empty list; `codkit package` then says that the type names no output and the operator reads the location from the packager's own output, which the command printed in full. For the same reason `build.packageDistributable` is empty here: the upstream task is the whole packaging of this family, and there is no second, product-supplied step after it.

p.VSCODE-PACKAGE-TARGET-CATALOG: The raw-bundle catalog is `windows-x64`, `windows-arm64`, `linux-x64`, `linux-arm64`, `linux-armhf`, `macos-x64`, `macos-arm64`, mapped one-to-one to the upstream `vscode-win32-*`, `vscode-linux-*` and `vscode-darwin-*` tasks. Windows hosts are measured for both Windows architectures and the Linux x64 cross-build; Linux ARM recipes remain Linux-hosted; both Intel and Apple-Silicon macOS recipes remain macOS-hosted. There is no upstream universal-mac task. Installer, signing, notarization, `.deb`, `.rpm` and `.snap` recipes are not raw-bundle aliases and are not claimed by this catalog. Windows recipes resolve `signtool.exe` from PATH or the newest installed Windows 10 SDK before spawning gulp.

tr.td: the only writer of JS into `out/`; on START it wipes `out/` (restart rarely and deliberately)
tsgo noEmit plus code generation into `src/`
40 projects; on start it wipes their `out/`
esbuild plus tsc noEmit of the copilot extension

p.DAEMON-TRAPS: Traps the wrapper implements: `npm run compile` and a restart of the transpile daemon wipe `out/`, so `build up` does not restart a living channel; before `npm install` in the tree the daemons must be stopped, so `build down --all` is invoked by the deps-advisory protocol; the upstream `watchd` scripts and our channels are mutually exclusive, so `up` refuses to start when a foreign watch process over the same tree is detected (probing by the command-line substrings `build/next/index.ts transpile --watch` and `gulp watch-`).

tr.td: `^Finished compilation with \d+ errors after \d+ ms$` (the counter is a 0/1 flag, not a number!)
`^(.+?)\((\d+),(\d+)\): error (TS\d+): (.+)$`; the real error count comes from `^Finished watch-client-noEmit .* with (\d+) errors\.$`
`^(?:\[\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}\] )?Starting compilation$` (the optional `[HH:mm:ss] ` prefix is live watch output; the bare legacy form is accepted too)

`^(?:\[\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}\] )?(?!\[)(.+?)\((\d+),(\d+)\): error (TS\d+): (.+)$` (the lookahead forbids swallowing a broken prefix without a space into the file path). There is NO aggregate count line: the lines `Finished extensions <project> with N errors.` are the totals of individual projects, not the total of the pass, and are ignored deliberately; `errorCountLine` is empty, and the authoritative count of the pass is the number of parsed diagnostics (`countFromSummary: false`)
`\[watch\] build finished` / `Found (\d+) errors?\. Watching for file changes`

p.FALSE-END-GUARDS: `falseEndGuards`: the lines `Finished compilation <id> with … errors` with a non-empty `<id>` come from the code-generation channels (`api-proposal-names`, `extension-point-names`), which print their markers on every change; a naive match yields false pass ends. M1 refinement: with strict `passEnd` expressions the guards are defence in depth and become load-bearing only when `passEnd` is weakened; the count lines are separated into their own data field `errorCountLine` (for typecheck/copilot the count line is not a diagnostic; extensions has NO count field, and the authority there is the parsed diagnostics, REPAIR-003/006).

p.TESTS-LAYER-SPLIT: **The split by runners.** `--runGlob` bypasses the regular layer exclusion of the upstream node runner, and a suite that brings up the workbench pulls in style sheets that node does not load; therefore `ci --profile build` runs the node runner over the glob `vs/<own>/**/test/{common,node}/**/*.test.js`, while the `test/browser` suites of the product, of the library and of the features are a mandatory protocol step outside `ci`: the upstream electron runner (`scripts/test.sh --runGlob 'vs/<own>/**/test/browser/**/*.test.js'`, under `xvfb-run` on a machine without a display), because a CI container without a display cannot make it mandatory for the profile.
